title: Needs a universal injury policy to compete with DraftKings and FanDuel
text: The app interface is smooth and building entries is fun, but PrizePicks drastically needs to improve its fairness guidelines regarding player injuries. Right now, the "Pregame Reboot List" feels completely random. It only protects a small, curated group of players each week. If you select a player who isn't on their lucky list and they get knocked out of the game in the 1st half, you are completely out of luck.The concept of using gimmicks like goblins and demons on the board is an okay concept for extra engagement, but it is completely irrelevant to the core issue of the injury policy. Adding fantasy elements doesn't make it right to have a restrictive list for certain players. Why only certain players?To make matters worse, their college football rules are incredibly restrictive compared to other sports. The CFB Reboot Policy only applies to players in AP Top 25 matchups or the official playoffs, leaving players in standard regular season games completely unprotected if they go down early.Major platforms like DraftKings and FanDuel are far more consistent and player-friendly when handling voided lines or injury disruptions across all games. PrizePicks needs a major overhaul to establish a fair standard: if any offensive player gets injured in the first half and never returns in the second half, they should automatically be rebooted. Until they make this rule universal instead of picking and choosing arbitrary games and players, the platform will continue to lag behind the transparency and fairness of its biggest competitors DraftKings & FanDuel.

title: Disappointing
text: I really think this app has the potential to be better and bigger than a lot of the other sportsbooks, but there are some things that seriously need improvement. One of the biggest issues is the live betting experience. The app can be extremely slow when matches are happening in real time, and sometimes the odds and game information feel delayed. Cash-out options can also be frustrating, especially when you’re winning significantly and the app doesn’t show a cash-out quickly enough or doesn’t update when you need it. For live sports, especially tennis, every point and every second matters. The app needs faster updates, more accurate live odds, quicker cash-out availability, and better real-time tracking. I see a lot of potential in this app, which is why I’m disappointed when things like this happen. If the developers can improve the speed, live betting, and cash-out system, I genuinely think this could compete with or even surpass some of the bigger sportsbooks.

title: Underdog cheats with voids & rescue
text: Underdog needs to explain their Rescue and Void rules — because this feels like a setup to avoid paying customers. I’m extremely disappointed with how Underdog handled my entries. I had multiple players hit exactly as selected, while another player was marked RESCUED. Instead of receiving any payout for the selections that actually won, Underdog simply returned my entry fee. That’s the problem: the customer takes all the risk when placing the entry, but when multiple selections hit, Underdog can use the Rescue/Void system to eliminate the payout. And the rules are not presented clearly enough for customers to understand exactly what happens to their winning selections when one player is rescued or voided. If three or four players hit, I expect a straightforward explanation of why those winning selections suddenly produce no winnings. I’ve also had a situation where a player returned to the game, participated, and was subsequently marked Rescued. If Underdog is going to apply Rescue after a player has returned to the game, then explain exactly why and show customers the rule being used to settle the entry. I’m not asking for special treatment. I’m asking Underdog to explain why winning selections are being reduced to nothing while the company keeps control of the settlement rules. If this is genuinely how the rules work, then make the rules crystal clear before customers put their money down, not after the ticket loses and Underdog decides how to grade it. Underdog: show the exact rule, show the calculation, and explain why my winning selections generated no payout. Don’t hide behind the word “Rescue.” Customers deserve transparency when real money is involved.
